keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). Infobox 'Kamerun partitioned: 20 July 1916' and 'Total: 89,526 km2'. The gazetteer resolves the Southern Cameroons (Nord-Ouest and Sud-Ouest regions of Cameroon) to about 48,300 km2, leaving about 41,000 km2 for the Northern Cameroons, 'two non-contiguous sections' on the Nigerian border; the gazetteer has no region 'British Cameroons' or 'Northern Cameroons', so the whole shape is a name it lacks.

ledger.note: 1916 (20 July): Britain and France divide German Kamerun. Infobox 'Kamerun partitioned: 20 July 1916'; 'British and French forces divided the German colony during World War I, with the British taking the smaller share'; capital Buea.

1922: the territory becomes a League of Nations mandate. Infobox status 'Class B League of Nations mandate under British administration (1922-1946)'; it is administered as two areas, Northern Cameroons and Southern Cameroons, 'still under the administration of Nigeria'.
1946 (6 December): the mandate becomes a UN trust territory. 'The United Nations approved the Trusteeship Agreements for British Cameroons to be governed by Britain on 6 December 1946.'

ledger.note: 1961 (1 June): the Northern Cameroons join Nigeria. After the UN plebiscite of 11 February 1961, in which 'the Muslim-majority Northern Area opted for union with Nigeria', 'Northern Cameroons became the Sardauna Province of Northern Nigeria on 1 June 1961'. The infobox gives 1 October 1961 for both integrations.

notes:
Written from one page (the British Cameroons article) within the small-state budget. Cliopatria has no row. The Nigeria dossier colony-and-protectorate-of-nigeria records the Cameroons as occupation (1916-1922) and a vassal relation (1922-1960) with counterpart british-cameroons; this is the mirror dossier.
Not settled: the Anglo-French boundary of 1916 and 1919 (not on the page), the Bakassi peninsula (not mentioned), the Northern Cameroons plebiscite of November 1959 (not on the page: only 11 February 1961 is), the separate areas of Northern and Southern Cameroons (the page gives only the 89,526 km2 total), and the 1954 and 1958 autonomy of the Southern Cameroons (not on the page). Gazetteer names needed: 'British Cameroons' and 'Northern Cameroons' (regions); the Southern Cameroons are drawn as the Nord-Ouest and Sud-Ouest admin-1 regions of Cameroon, a modern approximation.
